answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each identity post a non-transferable bond unlocked once by a verified human. A swarm of ten thousand wallets is no longer free: every new identity must stake ferrous tokens, slashed if peers catch it as a sock puppet. Cloning then costs scarce capital instead of cheap keyspace, so each fake identity is a small oasis of real expense and a thousand-agent attack costs a thousand times one honest member. Reputation accrues only to bonded identities, a knoll of trust copycats cannot climb without paying the toll.
